added.summary: A streamed video's player with `wait` holds the engine's clock on the web while it plays and its frame is not decoded yet (its chunk still downloading, or decoding behind), so the picture and its sound never part on a slow connection: the world ticks later instead. Off by default; executors always wait for each frame. Leave it off in a lockstep game.
A stream's seconds per chunk (`chunk 6` by default, rounded to whole key frame intervals): what a player downloads at a time.

fixed.summary: A streamed video is no longer downloaded whole when it loads. The cook splits each stream (and each rendition) into chunks from a key frame on; nothing is fetched until a player wants its frames, a playing player's chunks arrive up to four seconds ahead of it, and chunks no player needs are let go. A game can load all its footage in GameDesc.start and pays only for what plays; a paused player at a segment's start fetches and decodes just its first chunk. Re-cook to get chunked streams (og cook does it on its own); dump_stream lists each stream's chunks.
